title: Elastic Microburst Token Shepherd and Kernel-aware Duration Shaper
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Background: We still observe short-lived microbursts that cause kernel warm-up and uneven slot utilization which disproportionately increase P99 prefill+decode latency for mixed workloads. Existing admission and batch shaping layers handle steady-state well but de-optimize for transient, high-cardinality microbursts and heterogeneous kernel latencies.

Goal: Build a lightweight, kernel-aware admission layer — the 'Token Shepherd' — that (1) detects microburst episodes with sub-10ms sensitivity, (2) applies an elastic shaping envelope that amortizes bursts into microbatches without missing latency SLOs for high-priority traffic, and (3) cooperates with a Duration Shaper that predicts kernel runtime footprints per batch and enforces soft deadlines to avoid tail knots.

Design overview:
- Microburst detection: streaming EWMA + short-window histogram of arrival inter-arrival times per tenancy + request signature (seq_len, model_variant, priority). Use a Kalman-like filter to estimate instantaneous arrival rate spike factor.
- Token Shepherd (admission policy): when spike_factor > threshold, transform admission decisions with three levers: (a) elastic hold-and-release (timebox small delays up to 8ms parameterized by priority), (b) token fold (merge small requests with compatible kernel paths using attention-compatible padding rules), (c) graceful demotion (route non-critical requests to cheaper quantized kernels). Decisions are per-tenant and per-model-variant; state kept in in-memory ringlets per serving instance to avoid cross-instance coordination.
- Kernel-aware Duration Shaper: a lightweight predictive model (linear + kernel-profile lookup) that estimates per-batch GPU-time and memory transient for candidate kernel paths (e.g., fused attention vs. memory-sliced attention). The shaper uses these estimates to select an admission window that avoids creating batches that will violate soft decode deadlines or force kernel context-switches.
- Prefill/Decode scheduling integration: extend prefill pipeline to expose predicted decode-start-time and join-admission hooks. For requests that will be merged, maintain per-request KV-cache hints so merged outputs can be demultiplexed efficiently during decode.

Metrics and experiments:
- Primary metrics: P99 end-to-end prefill+decode latency, 95th decode-only latency, SLO violation rate (per-tenant), throughput (tokens/sec), kernel idle fraction, and cost-per-token.
- Canary experiments: run Token Shepherd off-path for 48h to collect decision logs; then enable on 5% traffic with feature-flagged knobs (max_hold_ms, merge_compatibility).
- A/B: compare baseline vs. Shepherd on high-cardinality tenant workloads and mixed short+long-gen workloads.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Added admission delay increases tail risk for very latency-sensitive calls; we mitigate via strict priority bypass and short max_hold_ms.
- Merging increases decode complexity (demultiplex), we keep merges limited to compatible model-variant+seq_len buckets and require pre-validated attention padding rules to preserve quality.
- Kernel estimate errors: we provision conservative buffers and keep a fallback that drops to decode-only admission when predictions are uncertain.

Rollout plan:
1) Off-path telemetry + synthetic load tests (2 weeks).
2) Canary 5% with conservative knobs (2 weeks).
3) 25% with dynamic knob tuning and automated rollback (1 week).
4) Gradual promotion to 100% with runtime metrics guardrails.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) P99 prefill+decode latency decreases by >=15% for identified microburst workloads without increasing P50 by >5%.
2) SLO violation rate for high-priority tenants remains <= baseline.
3) Kernel context-switch rate and short-lived kernel activations reduced by >=20% on canary hosts.
4) There is no regression in generation quality for merged requests (automated eval pass rate >= 99% on our eval prompts).
5) Rollback trigger: any tenant sees a >25% increase in SLO violations or customer complaints during canary.
